relations.rationale: Carrying boxes of gears wrapped in cloth is unrelated to the timing or nature of the morning maze session.
Leo driving the minibus has no bearing on spectators clapping at robot checkpoints.
Leo driving the minibus does not relate to Noor watching timers.
Leo driving the minibus is unrelated to Kira adjusting her robot's wheels.
Spending the night preparing batteries and sensors supports the claim that Nell was ready for the challenge.
Nell's preparation activities have no bearing on Ivo's height relative to Nell.
Being ready does not necessarily determine finishing order against Ivo, though readiness could support better performance.
Nell's readiness for the challenge has no direct bearing on the finishing order between Ivo and Kira.
Nell's readiness is unrelated to Leo being the oldest participant.
Nell's readiness has no bearing on the design complexity comparison between Kira and Ivo.
The maze navigation task described in claim 8 is elaborated by claim 9, which specifies guiding a robot through the course, supporting it as the same event.
Guiding robots through checkpoints supports the idea that spectators would clap as robots cleared them.
Each team guiding a robot through a course is consistent with and supports the idea that some robots were faster than others.
Teams guiding robots through a course supports the idea that Noor would note each completion attentively.
The robot course description has no bearing on the color of Noor's robot.
The maze task is unrelated to whether Noor's robot was easy to spot on a table.
The general maze task does not relate to the specific design comparison between Kira's and Ivo's robots.
Nell finishing ahead of Ivo and Ivo finishing ahead of Kira are consistent and together imply an order, supporting the transitive relation.
Nell finishing ahead of Ivo, combined with Ivo typically finishing ahead of Kira, supports Kira finishing after Nell, consistent with claim 18.
Finishing order in a robot competition has no bearing on relative ages.
